sanskrit_verse:
अक्षता च क्षता चैव पुनर्भूः संस्कृता पुनः /
स्वैरिणी या पतिं हित्वा सवर्णं कामतः श्रयेत् //
transliteration: akṣatā ca kṣatā caiva punarbhūḥ saṃskṛtā punaḥ / svairiṇī yā patiṃ hitvā savarṇaṃ kāmataḥ śrayet //
sph_interpretive_translation: A woman who, having abandoned her husband, approaches another man of the same varna out of desire—whether she be untouched, violated, or reborn through initiation—is again purified through ritual restoration.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in conscious choice and spiritual capacity, not in prior condition
Causation flows from intent and alignment, not past status
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by present awareness, not historical acts
Restoration logic operates through purification and reintegration, not exclusion
Consciousness alignment supersedes social or moral judgment
executable_legal_axioms: IF a woman abandons her spouse AND chooses union with another of equal varna, THEN initiate purification protocol
IF individual demonstrates intent to realign with dharma, THEN eligibility for restoration overrides prior condition
IF spiritual status changes via initiation, THEN prior violations are nullified by new consecration
IF consciousness is aligned with svadharma, THEN social penalties are void
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, the threshold of responsibility lies not in marital abandonment but in the current state of consciousness. Authority to restore lies with the spiritual capacity demonstrated post-initiation. Retribution has no place where realignment is evident.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that action follows intent. As intent shifts toward dharma, so too does consequence. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that purification follows contamination naturally when consciousness rises. Responsibility aligns with awareness; therefore, non-punitive restoration is the only lawful response.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Vedic purification rites upon declaration of realignment
Assign completion process for integration into community without stigma
Conduct svadhyaya session for reestablishment of personal dharma
Establish mentorship under qualified guru for sustained consciousness elevation
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores consciousness above condition, purifies intent beyond history, and affirms that reality itself enforces justice through alignment—not punishment.
